items.title: Karnataka’s Beda Bro campaign targets Gen Z, but is the message getting through?
items.summary: We have never received an email about this particular campaign that has been going on by the government of Karnataka. So I was quite surprised.” Karan, a fourth-year Social Sciences major, is closely involved in substance-abuse awareness work on his campus, at a Bengaluru university that keeps close contact with Karnataka police on drug-related issues. Yet, when asked about the state government’s Beda Bro campaign, he said he had not heard of it. The campaign is a government initiative designed as a social message geared towards helping young people unapologetically say "No" to drugs. Spearheaded by Priyank Kharge, Minister for Home, Information Technology & Biotechnology, and e-Governance, it was launched alongside Operation RISE (Refuse, Inform, Support, Empower) on June 30, as part of its anti-drug efforts. Since its launch, the campaign has been rolled out through police events, college programmes, awareness activities, and partnerships with private institutions. In Dakshina Kannada , Mysuru , and Belagavi , district police and local officials have held briefings, college events, and documentary screenings combining enforcement, awareness, and counselling support. items.title: BJP leader Nainar Nagendran targets Vijay’s mother, faces backlash
items.summary: Tamil Nadu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president Nainar Nagendran has sparked a political controversy after making a personal remark involving Chief Minister and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) chief C Joseph Vijay’s mother. Speaking at the launch of Oru Naadu 2.0 in Chennai on Saturday, August 15, Nagendran said, “In the legislative assembly, some are searching for a father. But only by asking the mother at home can one know who the father is.” He added, “Who will reveal if he is being searched for in the Assembly? This is the situation of the present government.” Nagendran’s remarks were in response to an earlier comment by Vijay in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly. Vijay had, on June 23, narrated a story about an elderly man looking for a child’s father and asking, “Where’s your father? I can’t find him.” The remark was understood as a veiled reference to former Chief Minister MK Stalin, who had lost his Assembly seat in the 2026 election. Nagendran appeared to turn Vijay’s “father” reference back on him.
